title: Mouthpiece lay, reeds, and his father's goat-horn reed
summary: Talk of mouthpiece lay and matching soft reeds to wide lays; Lewis's father tried to make a reed from goat horn.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Um, can you tell me anything about, uh, mouth, the mouthpiece or the lay? You know the lay, what they call the lay on the mouthpiece? What, what, do you have any feelings about that? Yeah, I have two mouthpieces I use now.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

I would like a wide layer. A wide layer, I could use a soft reed. A bind is bind with the mouthpiece. If you've got a close reed, you use a hard mouthpiece. Try to slide. Yeah, the layer you use a hard reed. If you've got a wide layer, use a soft reed.

I believe Raymond Burke used to scrape the mouthpiece, the layer of the mouthpiece on the ground to make it wider and that kind of thing. Did you ever do anything like that? No, no, no. I never tried.
I tried, in fact my daddy was living in a goat horn. I never heard a horn of a goat to make a reed and couldn't get nothing out of it.
Your father tried to make that?

He didn't have anything to do. He would turn it up. He scrapped it, but he couldn't get it to the guitar. He would produce a tom. There was something that's on order to me. Like this classic reed. Just sell it now.
Did he do that for you? No, he doesn't have anything to do. Did he play any instruments himself?
No, no. He just took over and reed and sell it. Sorry it was me. He didn't believe none of my folks ever feel anything.
Did you ever try to make a reed yourself? No. Did you know any musicians and you were on the driver who ever did try to make reed? No. You never heard of that?
